text.p: Portuguese police detectives want more danger money and are threatening to strike for two days at the end of December if their demands are not met by mid-month, the president of their union said on Wednesday.

"Our members are facing increasing danger from drug-trafficking, terrorism, violent crime and the smuggling of toxic waste," Manuel Carvalho, head of the Union for Criminal Investigation of the Judicial Police, told Reuters.
He said that if Justice Minister Jose Vera Jardim did not accept the unions' demands, senior detectives would hand in their arms on December 18 and strike on December 30 and 31.
"Our demands are urgent and should be resolved before the end of the year," he said.
Another police source said a strike by the union, which represents just over 1,000 detectives across the country, could severely disrupt activity by the national police force.
